albums.blurb: Recorded in Paris over two nights in December 1957, this is the score Miles Davis improvised for Louis Malle's debut feature Elevator to the Gallows, leading a quintet of Barney Wilen, René Urtreger, Pierre Michelot and Kenny Clarke while loops of the film were projected in the studio. Sitting between Relaxin' and Milestones in his discography, its sparse, scale-based brooding is often heard as a dry run for the modal turn that produced Kind of Blue the following year, and the whole record is instrumental small-group jazz.
albums.reception: AllMusic's retrospective review rates it four and a half stars, and its American release as side one of the 1959 Columbia LP Jazz Track brought Davis a 1960 Grammy nomination for Best Jazz Performance, Solo or Small Group.

albums.album: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You
albums.blurb: Big Thief's fifth studio album and their most expansive: a twenty-track double LP on 4AD, assembled from five 2020 sessions in Westhampton, upstate New York, Topanga Canyon, the Colorado Rockies and Tucson, each with a different engineer. Adrianne Lenker's songwriting ranges from hushed acoustic folk to country stomps and crunchy full-band rock, with drummer James Krivchenia producing.
albums.reception: It reached number 31 on the Billboard 200 and number 15 on the UK albums chart, and was nominated for Best Alternative Music Album at the 65th Grammy Awards, where its single "Certainty" was also nominated for Best Alternative Music Performance.

albums.blurb: Vanishing Twin are a London ensemble led by singer and multi-instrumentalist Cathy Lucas, formerly of Fanfarlo, with bassist Susumu Mukai (alias Zongamin) and Italian percussionist Valentina Magaletti. Ookii Gekkou — Japanese for "big moonlight" — is their third album, written and recorded during lockdown and released on Fire Records, folding exotica, library music, afrofunk and Stereolab-style motorik pop into their most rhythm-forward record.
albums.reception: BrooklynVegan named it an Album of the Week, hearing the band trade the sharper edges of 2019's The Age of Immunology for a funkier, more danceable sound, and Norman Records' staff review scored it 8/10.
